cards.question: Does chart-only GRPO keep its reasoning past update 2,000? The photos + charts model collapsed to about 10 tokens between updates 1,750 and 2,000 of 2,844, while the chart-only model stopped at 1,844, so mixing and training length are confounded.
cards.change: 2,844 updates instead of 1,844 on ChartQA alone: the mixture's horizon and learning-rate schedule
cards.predicted: Holds. End-of-run dev answers stay above half the 1,844-update model's length and dev accuracy within 2 points of it: chart questions reward reasoning, and the collapse came from the photo questions' pressure toward short answers. Answers keep shortening slowly, as they did from 198 tokens at update 300 to 162 at 1,844.
cards.holds_if: end-of-run dev tokens >= 50% of the baseline's and dev accuracy >= baseline - 2 points
cards.if_holds: Mixing caused the collapse: run the prompt-routing and ratio cards.
cards.if_not: Long-run RL instability, not mixing: no ratio cards; the finding becomes when to stop.
cards.why: Observed: 1,000 more updates leave dev accuracy where it was (75.8) and answers do not collapse. They lengthen after update 1,250 (137 to 179 tokens), so the predicted slow shortening was wrong.
cards.implies: The collapse comes from mixing, not length. Next: prompt routing and one other ratio. Chart-only training gains nothing past 1,844 updates.

cards.question: Does SFT on reasoning traces close GRPO's lead on ChartQA, given the same information RL has: the model's own samples and the checker?
cards.change: SFT on one correct reasoning sample per question from Instruct 2B, instead of GRPO
cards.predicted: Holds. GRPO stays at least 2 points ahead on dev. Correct traces lift SFT above Instruct and keep its reasoning, but one offline pass cannot sharpen the way repeated on-policy updates do.
cards.holds_if: SFT on traces ends at least 2 dev points below the chart-only GRPO model
cards.if_holds: The chart win stands against SFT on reasoning traces.
cards.if_not: The win comes from the reasoning targets rather than from RL, and the root claim changes.
cards.why: Observed: 70.2 against GRPO's 75.8 on dev (-5.6 [-8.6, -2.6]), and 1.6 above Instruct. Answers stay long (184 tokens). Trained on the 6,401 questions with a correct sample.
cards.implies: The chart win stands against SFT on the same information RL has.

cards.question: Does SFT on a larger model's reasoning traces close GRPO's lead on ChartQA?
cards.change: SFT on one correct reasoning sample per question from Instruct 8B, instead of GRPO
cards.predicted: Holds. GRPO stays at least 2 points ahead on dev, with this arm at or above SFT on 2B's traces: a stronger teacher improves the targets, and the student still gets one offline pass.
cards.holds_if: SFT on 8B traces ends at least 2 dev points below the chart-only GRPO model
cards.if_holds: The chart win stands even against a larger teacher's traces.
cards.if_not: A larger teacher can replace RL at 2B on charts; compare against 2B self-traces to separate teacher size from targets.
cards.why: Observed: 71.8 against GRPO's 75.8 on dev (-4.0 [-7.2, -0.8]), close to the teacher's own 72.6. Trained on the 6,164 questions with a correct sample.
cards.implies: The chart win stands even against a larger teacher's traces, and offline SFT lands near its teacher rather than past it.

cards.question: Does a mixed model keep chart reasoning when each dataset rolls out under its own prompt?
cards.change: Photos roll out under the short prompt and charts under the reasoning prompt, on the mixture's pool and 2,844 updates
cards.predicted: Holds. Chart answers stay above half the chart-only length and ChartQA dev within 2 points of it: photo questions no longer have reasoning to delete, so their pressure toward short answers is gone.
cards.holds_if: end-of-run ChartQA dev tokens >= 50% of the chart-only control's and dev accuracy >= its accuracy - 2 points
cards.if_holds: One model can keep both behaviors under routed prompts; apply the 8B gate.
cards.if_not: Sharing weights is enough to carry the pressure across prompts; a mixed hero run is off the table.
cards.why: Observed: chart answers stay at 151 tokens (84% of chart-only) and ChartQA dev ends 1.4 points below chart-only [-3.8, 1.0]. Proposed: under the short prompt, photo questions have no reasoning to delete, so nothing pushes chart answers shorter.
cards.implies: One model keeps both behaviors, but its dev macro is 2.1 points below the specialists' [-3.8, -0.5] and charts are 2.2 below, so it fails the 8B gate (results/gate.json). Specialists go forward.

cards.question: Does a mixed model keep chart reasoning under one prompt when photos are only 10% of the pool?
cards.change: 90% charts and 10% photos instead of 65% and 35%, all under the reasoning prompt, 2,844 updates
cards.predicted: Does not hold. Fewer photos delay the collapse, as 65% charts delayed it by about 1,500 updates, but one prompt still pays for short answers on some questions and 2,844 updates are long enough to reach it.
cards.holds_if: end-of-run ChartQA dev tokens >= 50% of the chart-only control's and dev accuracy >= its accuracy - 2 points
cards.if_holds: Ratio alone protects chart reasoning; check what it costs on photos.
cards.if_not: Ratio only delays the collapse; routing is the recipe to carry forward.
cards.why: Observed: chart answers stay at 188 tokens and ChartQA dev ends 0.4 points below chart-only [-3.0, 2.0]; the predicted late collapse did not come. Photos answered under the shared reasoning prompt end 6.3 points below the photo specialist.
cards.implies: Ratio alone keeps chart reasoning but costs photos: dev macro is 3.3 points below the specialists' [-6.7, 0.0], so it fails the 8B gate (results/gate.json). Specialists go forward.

cards.question: Does a mixed model keep chart reasoning under one prompt that lets it decide whether to reason?
cards.change: All rollouts under the winning adaptive prompt, on the mixture's pool and 2,844 updates
cards.predicted: Does not hold. The prompt gives permission to skip reasoning but the reward still pays for short answers on photos, and the mixed model already separated the families for 1,750 updates under the plain prompt before it collapsed.
cards.holds_if: end-of-run ChartQA dev tokens >= 50% of the chart-only control's and dev accuracy >= its accuracy - 2 points
cards.if_holds: One model and one prompt keep both behaviors; this is the recipe to carry to the 8B gate.
cards.if_not: The prompt alone does not protect chart reasoning; compare with routing.
cards.why: Observed before any training: under all three wordings Instruct 2B wrote longer answers on VQAv2 than on ChartQA (ratio 0.68-0.88, the rule needed 2) and lost 3.8-8.4 points on ChartQA and 13.9-21.9 on VQAv2 against the better of short and reasoning.
cards.implies: An instruction alone does not make the released model reason selectively. Routing is the mixture recipe to test.

cards.question: When the image contradicts the usual answer, does each method still follow the image?
cards.change: Score existing arms on VQAv2 complementary pairs: pair accuracy (both right) and same-answer rate (one answer for two images whose answers differ)
cards.predicted: Holds. SFT raises the same-answer rate over Instruct, since it also learns which answers are likely for a question; GRPO from Instruct does not, and its pair-accuracy gain is at least its single-question gain.
cards.holds_if: SFT's same-answer rate is above Instruct's with a 95% interval above zero, and GRPO's is not
cards.if_holds: A new grounding result: RL follows the image when it disagrees with the prior, SFT less so.
cards.if_not: Both methods lean on priors alike; grounding differences show only in the black-image test.
cards.why: Observed on 978 pairs (results/pairs.json): SFT's same-answer rate is 1.2 points below Instruct's [-3.0, +0.5], not above; every short-answer model gives one answer to both images 21-22% of the time. SFT has the best pair accuracy (57.8 against Instruct's 54.0, +3.8 [+1.9, +5.7]).
cards.implies: On photos, neither method makes the model answer from habit more than Instruct does. The prior effect seen with black images on medical sets does not show on VQAv2 pairs.

cards.question: How much does answer-only SFT on InfoVQA's training questions add to Instruct?
cards.change: SFT on InfoVQA's sft role, one epoch of short answers
cards.predicted: Holds. SFT adds at least 3 dev points over Instruct: the text is in the image, so the gain is InfoVQA's answer conventions (which span, units, rounding), which labels teach directly.
cards.holds_if: SFT's dev ANLS is at least Instruct's + 3 points
cards.if_holds: SFT is a strong document baseline; GRPO is measured against it.
cards.if_not: Instruct already follows InfoVQA's conventions; what is left for either method is sharpening.
cards.why: Observed: SFT ends 1.6 dev points above Instruct [-1.3, 4.4] (63.6 to 65.2 ANLS; +2.7 at update 500), with answers still 4 to 5 tokens. Proposed: Instruct already answers in InfoVQA's form, so labels have little left to teach at this pixel budget.
cards.implies: Answer-only SFT adds little on infographics; GRPO is compared against an SFT arm close to Instruct.

cards.question: On a document task where reasoning does not pay, does GRPO beat SFT?
cards.change: GRPO from Instruct under the short prompt, 2,000 updates, instead of SFT
cards.predicted: Holds. GRPO ends within 2 dev points of SFT. Reasoning does not pay here and the short prompt leaves no answer form to change, so RL can only sharpen what Instruct already samples (79.6% with 8 samples against 66.6% greedy), and SFT gets about as far from labels.
cards.holds_if: GRPO's dev ANLS is within 2 points of SFT's
cards.if_holds: Documents join photos: where reasoning does not pay, RL and SFT end level.
cards.if_not: Above: RL's edge reaches a task where reasoning does not pay, and the root claim widens. Below: labels carry more than sharpening here.
cards.why: Observed: GRPO ends 1.8 dev points below SFT [-4.5, 0.9] and 0.2 below Instruct; dev ANLS stays between 61.6 and 63.7 for all 2,000 updates. Train reward moves 0.63 to 0.65 while groups with one reward for all 8 samples rise from 75% to 89%. Proposed: the sampled spread on a span is noise around one reading, so RL makes the model surer without making it right.
cards.implies: Documents join photos: where reasoning does not pay, RL and SFT end level. Instruct's pass@8 lead over greedy (about 13 points) did not turn into a gain, so headroom alone does not predict RL's.

cards.question: Does GRPO add to SFT on InfoVQA?
cards.change: GRPO from the SFT model, with the same 2,000 updates
cards.predicted: Holds. SFT → GRPO ends between 1 point below and 3 points above SFT on dev: RL sharpens what the SFT model samples, as it added 1.4 on SLAKE.
cards.holds_if: SFT → GRPO's dev ANLS is within -1 to +3 points of SFT's
cards.if_holds: RL after SFT polishes, as on SLAKE.
cards.if_not: Above: RL adds more after SFT than a polish. Below: RL undoes part of what SFT taught.
cards.why: Observed: SFT -> GRPO ends 0.9 dev points above SFT [-1.4, 3.3] (66.1 ANLS), the best InfoVQA arm and 2.5 above Instruct.
cards.implies: RL after SFT keeps what SFT taught and adds a little; on infographics neither method moves Instruct far.

cards.question: Can answer-only SFT on ViRL39K reach what Instruct gets by reasoning?
cards.change: SFT on ViRL39K's sft role, one epoch of short answers
cards.predicted: Holds. SFT under the short prompt ends below Instruct's reasoning score on dev: a final answer to a math problem cannot be read off the image, and answer-only labels teach no steps.
cards.holds_if: SFT's dev score (short prompt) is below Instruct's (reasoning prompt, 2,048 tokens)
cards.if_holds: Reasoning carries what labels alone cannot; GRPO is measured against this SFT arm.
cards.if_not: Labels teach this task without reasoning, and the reasoning-pays branch weakens.
cards.why: Observed: SFT ends 9.8 dev points above Instruct's reasoning score [4.8, 14.8] (43.0 to 52.8) and 12.2 above its short score, with 3-token answers. It gains on every answer form over Instruct's short answers: multiple choice +11.3, numbers +11.9, text +19.7. Proposed: one epoch of 33,635 answers teaches the dataset's answer conventions and answer priors; how much of it needs the image is not measured.
cards.implies: Answer-only SFT is a strong baseline here: GRPO needs about 54.8 on dev, 11.8 above Instruct's reasoning, for its card to hold. A black-image score of the SFT model would show how much of the gain is priors.

cards.question: On a second dataset where reasoning pays, does GRPO beat SFT?
cards.change: GRPO from Instruct under the reasoning prompt, 2,048-token answers, 2,000 updates, instead of SFT
cards.predicted: Holds. GRPO ends at least 2 dev points above SFT, each under its training prompt: reasoning adds 17 points for Instruct here, RL keeps and sharpens it, and answer-only SFT cannot use it.
cards.holds_if: GRPO's dev score (reasoning, 2,048 tokens) is at least SFT's (short) + 2 points
cards.if_holds: The chart result repeats on a second reasoning dataset: where reasoning pays, RL beats SFT.
cards.if_not: The chart win does not generalize; the root claim narrows to charts.
cards.why: Observed: GRPO ends 7.0 dev points above SFT [1.8, 12.2] (52.8 to 59.8) and 16.8 above Instruct's reasoning score (43.0). Answers cut off by the 2,048-token limit fall from 30% to 6% and shorten to 626 tokens; dev rises from 51.0 at update 250 to 59.8 at 2,000. The estimate written before the result (52-62 from learning to finish alone) holds.
cards.implies: A second dataset where reasoning pays and RL beats SFT, as predicted: the Milestone 2 replace rule is met. Next control: SFT on reasoning examples, which settled ChartQA.

cards.question: Does GRPO after answer-only SFT bring reasoning back on ViRL39K?
cards.change: GRPO from the SFT model under the reasoning prompt, with the same 2,000 updates
cards.predicted: Holds. SFT -> GRPO ends at least 2 dev points above SFT, each under its training prompt, but below GRPO from Instruct: RL can only sharpen the reasoning the SFT model still samples.
cards.holds_if: SFT -> GRPO's dev score (reasoning, 2,048 tokens) is at least SFT's (short) + 2 points
cards.if_holds: RL restores reasoning after answer-only SFT; the order SFT then RL is safe here too.
cards.if_not: Answer-only SFT removed reasoning that RL cannot recover within 2,000 updates.
cards.why: Observed: 54.8 dev under the reasoning prompt, 2.0 above SFT [-1.4, 5.6], with 13-token answers: RL taught the answer tag, not reasoning. It ends 5.0 below GRPO from Instruct. The rule reads held on the point estimate, but the interval crosses zero and the predicted mechanism failed.
cards.implies: Answer-only SFT removes the reasoning RL needs here; where reasoning pays, start RL from the base model. The opposite of medicine, where SFT then RL was best.

cards.question: Does SFT on Instruct's own correct reasoning close GRPO's lead on ViRL39K?
cards.change: SFT on one correct reasoning sample per question from Instruct 2B, instead of GRPO
cards.predicted: Holds. GRPO stays at least 2 dev points ahead (SFT on reasoning at or below 57.8). Correct traces keep reasoning and teach finishing, but one offline pass over Instruct's samples cannot sharpen the way 2,000 on-policy updates do; on ChartQA RL led the same control by 5.6.
cards.holds_if: SFT on reasoning ends at least 2 dev points below GRPO (reasoning prompt, 2,048 tokens)
cards.if_holds: The math win stands against SFT on the same information RL has: it comes from RL, not from reasoning targets.
cards.if_not: Reasoning targets carry the math gain; on ViRL39K the root claim credits reasoning, not RL.
